defs.def: a number of people standing or sitting next to each other in a line; a number of objects arranged in a line 一排；一列；一行

ex.s: Rather than watering rows of soil, the system provides just the right amount to each plant.
ex.t: 系统不是浇灌一排排土壤，而是为每株植物提供恰到好处的水量。

ex.s: Moving carefully through the darkness, she passes row upon row of rose plants.
ex.t: 她小心翼翼地穿过黑暗，经过一排又一排的玫瑰植物。

ex.s: She moves carefully through the darkness and passes many rows of rose plants.
ex.t: 她小心翼翼地穿过黑暗，经过许多排玫瑰植物。

ex.s: There was a row of trees near his friend’s house, and one of them was much taller than the others.
ex.t: 他朋友家旁边有一排树，其中一棵比其他树高得多。

ex.s: Complete the table.Then write three headings that can categorise the information in the first row.
ex.t: 完成表格。然后写出三个可以将第一行信息分类的标题。

defs.def: a line of seats in a cinema/movie theater, etc. （剧院、电影院等的）一排座位

ex.s: The traffic signals along Factoria Boulevard in Bellevue, Washington, generally don't flash the same length of green twice in a row, especially at rush hour.
ex.t: 华盛顿州贝尔维尤市法克托里亚大道上的交通信号灯通常不会连续两次亮相同时长的绿灯，尤其是在高峰时段。

ex.s: Locating in front of the Falls, the hotel provides a front-row view of the Canadian Horseshoe Falls.
ex.t: 酒店位于瀑布前方，可以正面观赏加拿大马蹄瀑布。

defs.def: a complete line of stitches in knitting or crochet （编织中的）针行，一整行
an act of rowing a boat; the period of time spent doing this 划船（时间）
if sth happens several times in a row, it happens in exactly the same way each time, and nothing different happens in the time between 连续几次地

ex.s: If you miss two PASS sessions in a row, you will be deregistered and your place will be given to someone on the waiting list.
ex.t: 如果你连续错过两次PASS课程，你将被取消注册，你的位置将给候补名单上的人。

ex.s: they give their places to othersD. they miss two sessions in a row
ex.t: 他们把位置让给别人D. 他们连续两次缺席课程

defs.def: if sth happens for several days, etc. in a row, it happens on each of those days 接连几天（等）地
to move a boat through water using oars (= long wooden poles with flat ends) 划（船）
to take sb somewhere in a boat with oars 划船送（某人）
a serious disagreement between people, organizations, etc. about sth 严重分歧；纠纷
a noisy argument between two or more people 吵架；争吵

ex.s: If a customer is rude or difficult, just think "Maybe she’s had a row with her husband.
ex.t: 如果顾客粗鲁或难缠，就想"也许她和丈夫吵架了。

defs.def: a loud unpleasant noise 大的噪音
